title: Midnight pulse — Sparrow relay summary
content:
High-level summary:

- Short summary: Between 04:10–04:40 UTC we observed a transient latency and 5xx spike originating from the token-serving path. Root cause is likely KV cache thrash combined with aggressive autoscaler churn on the beam-autoscaler pool. Incident ID: INC-2026-07-30-0421.
- Impact: ~18 minutes of degraded p95 latency (spike to ~800ms) for the token/generate route; elevated 5xx rate peaked at ~6% across the traffic slice; internal retries amplified pressure on downstream caches. No customer SLA breaches recorded for the Dedicated customers, but increased error surface for hosted API free tier.

Timeline (UTC):
- 04:08 — Alert: p95 token/generate latency breach (alert threshold 200ms) triggered.
- 04:10 — Pager to on-call (me). Began triage.
- 04:12 — Noted autoscaler scaling loop in beam-autoscaler logs: frequent add/remove events (5 events in 3m).
- 04:14 — Observed KV cache eviction rate spike in kv-proxy metrics and thrash in memcache-client.
- 04:16 — Rolled an emergency mitigation: temporarily pinned beam-autoscaler to min_instances=4 for the pool serving token/generate (manual override).
- 04:18 — Latency started to flatten; p95 down from 800ms to ~300ms. Error rate still elevated.
- 04:22 — Increased cache TTL for token-prefix entries from 30s -> 120s as a temporary measure (applied via feature-flag toggle).
- 04:28 — Error rate dropped below 1%. Observability graphs show KV hit-rate recovering.
- 04:40 — Traffic normalized; autoscaler returned to stable behavior after 20m.

Systems observed:
- route-router (token/generate route) — request fanout behavior looked normal.
- kv-proxy / memcache-client — high eviction/SET rates, decreased hit-rate.
- beam-autoscaler — flapping due to tightly coupled CPU-based autoscaling with short window.
- retry-middleware — contributed to amplified load, exponential backoff not engaged due to bug in middleware v1.11.

Immediate mitigations performed:
1) Manual pin of autoscaler for affected pool (min_instances=4) to force capacity stability.
2) Increased cache TTL for token-prefix keys via runtime flag.
3) Temporary throttle on internal retries (set retry multiplier to 0.5 for token/generate) to slow amplification.
4) Added short-term circuit-breaker on kv-proxy for high-set rate (reject new non-critical sets).

Preliminary root-cause hypothesis:
- Combination of two interacting factors: sudden spike in concurrent token generation requests from a small customer cohort + a recently merged autoscaler change that reduced stabilization window to 30s. The short stabilization window caused rapid scale down/up cycles which increased cache miss rates and caused memcache to see many SETs, thrashing the eviction algorithm and increasing tail latency. Retry middleware then amplified load further.

Follow-ups / action items (owners):
- SRE: formal postmortem write-up (include detailed timelines and graphs) — owner: Asha Patel — due: 2026-08-03.
- Platform: revert autoscaler stabilization tuning or make it workload-aware (PR + canary) — owner: Miguel Ortega — due: 2026-08-06.
- Platform: add a histogram-based cooldown check to beam-autoscaler (prevent scale decisions when p95 oscillates) — owner: Lina Zhang — due: 2026-08-14.
- Cache: investigate eviction policy and introduce adaptive TTL for hot prefixes — owner: Tomas Becker — due: 2026-08-10.
- SDK/devs: investigate retry middleware bug that prevents exponential backoff engagement in v1.11 — owner: API SDK team (linked in JIRA) — due: 2026-08-05.
- Observability: create a Grafana panel that surfaces autoscaler churn rate and correlated cache miss-rate (alert candidate) — owner: Observability team — due: 2026-08-04.

Runbook draft: kv-cache-thrash (rough steps, keep minimal for on-call):
1) Detect: Alert when cache eviction rate > 2000 evictions/min AND p95 latency > 300ms for > 5m.
2) Confirm: tail kv-proxy logs for high SET rates and correlated memcache errors.
3) Mitigate fast:
   a) Apply runtime flag to increase TTL for hot prefixes (+90–300s) for immediate relief.
   b) Pin autoscaler min_instances to a safe floor for the affected pool for 15–30m.
   c) Throttle non-essential sets at kv-proxy by rejecting low-priority writes.
4) Stabilize: monitor hit-rate and p95 for 10m after mitigations. If stable, gradually revert flags and remove manual pins.
5) Post-incident: open ticket to tune eviction policy / increase capacity for predicted hot prefixes.

Notes to incoming on-call (what I would do if I were you):
- If you see p95 > 500ms, first check autoscaler churn and cache eviction metrics side-by-side (Grafana panel: kv-cache + autoscaler-churn).
- If autoscaler is flapping, pin min_instances immediately to stop scale-down loops; reduce non-critical retries; do not blow away caches with global TTL changes unless necessary.
- If unsure, call platform pager (Miguel) before making cross-cluster config changes.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Which customer(s) triggered the initial concurrency spike? Need request-id traces tied back to customer id (privacy — use internal lookup).
- How did the new autoscaler tuning PR make it past canary without catching churn? Possible coverage gap in canary workload.
- Does memcache eviction policy need a different sizing or a replacement for hot prefixes (LRU vs. TinyLFU)?

Attachments & references:
- JIRA SRE-1247 (incident ticket, contains raw logs and initial annotations)
- Grafana: latency panel (kv-cache & token/generate) — /d/latency/kv-cache-2026-07-30
- Slack thread snapshot: #sre-incident-archive/2026-07-30-0421

Notes to self / working thoughts (scratchpad):
- Consider an autoscaler change that factors in cache-hit-rate as a negative signal for scale-down.
- Short-term: add a circuit-breaker on retry-middleware when downstream 5xx crosses threshold.
- Remember to capture heap snapshots from kv-proxy if thrash reoccurs (low overhead snapshot mode exists).

Incoming on-call checklist (quick):
- Check active alerts -> acknowledge if assigned.
- Open INC-2026-07-30-0421 for context.
- Look at autoscaler churn + cache eviction graphs.
- If latency > 400ms: pin autoscaler and increase TTL.
- After stabilizing: update runbook with the exact thresholds we observed.

Signed-off: Asha (night relay)

— end of relay —
